questions.q:
NITI Aayog's Fiscal Health Index 2026 uses five pillars. Consider the following pairs:
Pillar : What it measures
1. Fiscal Prudence : Deficit discipline and adherence to FRBM norms
2. Quality of Expenditure : Long-run ability to service debt
3. Revenue Mobilization : Own tax and non-tax revenue capacity
4. Debt Sustainability : Size and composition of outstanding liabilities
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 3 are right. Pair 2 is wrong: Quality of Expenditure compares productive spending such as capital works, health and education with salaries, pensions and interest. Pair 4 is wrong: size and composition belong to the Debt Index, while Debt Sustainability concerns long-run servicing ability through interest-to-revenue ratios and primary balance trends. The look-alike debt pillars are the likely trap here.

questions.q:
With reference to the new national accounts series released by MoSPI with 2022-23 as the base year, consider the following statements:
1. Double deflation, which deflates input prices as well as output prices, is now used in manufacturing and agriculture in place of single deflation.
2. 2022-23 was chosen because it was the year in which the COVID-19 disruption peaked.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: double deflation removes price effects from inputs and outputs separately, giving a truer measure of real value added than deflating output alone. Statement 2 is wrong: 2022-23 was chosen as the most recent normal year after the disruption of 2019 to 2021. The series also brings in GST, e-Vahan and PFMS data. The National Statistical Office revises the base roughly every five to ten years, following the UN System of National Accounts.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 33-34; Shankar IAS pp. 61-64

questions.q: Which one of the following best describes where Digital Public Infrastructure sits in the digital economy?
o: An intermediate layer between physical infrastructure such as networks and data centres and sectoral applications such as telehealth
The end-user applications sold by private firms for e-commerce and remote education
A regulatory layer of statutes that governs data protection and platform liability
The physical layer of towers, cables and servers that carries all digital traffic
questions.e: DPI sits in the middle. Beneath it lie connectivity, devices, servers and cloud, and above it are sector applications like e-commerce, social protection, remote education and telehealth. Hence it is not the physical layer or private end-use applications. Nor is it law, although the DPDP Act, 2023 regulates data use on it. This layered model explains why India can offer it to other countries as a scalable template.

questions.q:
Consider the following countries:
1. Bhutan
2. France
3. Japan
4. Malaysia
5. Qatar
As reported in early 2026, how many of the above were listed among countries where UPI is live?
questions.e: Bhutan, France and Qatar are on the reported list, along with the UAE, Singapore, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Mauritius, totalling eight. Japan and Malaysia are not on it. Overseas acceptance helps Indian travellers and remittances and supports India's digital diplomacy, which also includes agreements with 24 countries on India Stack and DPI cooperation. Rankings and lists may change, so the date matters.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 25-27; Shankar IAS p. 19

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Essential Commodities (Amendment) Act, 2020 no longer stands on the statute book.
Statement-II: Stock limits on wheat were imposed in 2023 and revised in 2025 under the Essential Commodities Act.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct, but the second does not explain the first. The 2020 amendment was repealed through the Farm Laws Repeal Act, 2021, as a result of farmer protests, and its removal is a matter of parliamentary action. Later wheat limits simply show the parent Act in use. Many summaries still describe the 2020 thresholds as if they were current, so readers should check this carefully.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 66-68; Farm Laws Repeal Act, 2021 is static

questions.q:
With reference to biogas, consider the following statements:
1. Methane is its largest component.
2. It is produced by bacteria in the presence of plentiful oxygen.
3. The slurry left behind can serve as organic fertiliser.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: methane is about 55 to 60 per cent, with carbon dioxide next, and bio-slurry can reduce chemical fertiliser use. Statement 2 is wrong: production needs anaerobic digestion, without oxygen, in airtight biodigesters, landfills or sewage treatment plants. Interest revived during the LPG crunch as biogas can diversify an import-exposed mix and help with rural waste management.

questions.q:
With reference to export support during the West Asia disruption, consider the following statements:
1. ECGC Ltd is wholly owned by the Government of India under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
2. The Export-Import Bank of India is the implementing agency for RELIEF under the Export Promotion Mission.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: ECGC, set up in 1957, insures exporters against credit risk. Statement 2 is wrong: ECGC itself implements RELIEF, giving up to 100 per cent cover to exporters already insured with it and up to 95 per cent to those taking cover in the next three months. EXIM Bank is a separate statutory lender that finances trade, whereas ECGC provides insurance and guarantees, which is what exporters needed during the disruption.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 38-39; EXIM Bank's separate role is static

questions.q:
Statement-I: Micron's ATMP facility at Sanand, inaugurated in 2026, does not carry out wafer fabrication.
Statement-II: Assembly, Test, Marking and Packaging is a back-end stage that works on wafers fabricated elsewhere.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct and linked. Chipmaking has a front end, where circuits are etched on wafers in a fab, and a back end, where dies are assembled, tested, marked and packaged. The Sanand unit belongs to the back end, which is why fabs form a separate scheme under the India Semiconductor Mission. ATMP is close to OSAT, Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test, the model of firms that do such work for chip designers and fabs.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 29-30; front-end and back-end distinction is static

questions.q: MOSIP, which more than 25 nations are adopting or exploring, is best described as
o: an international treaty on the protection of biometric data
a cross-border payment gateway linking central banks in South Asia
a global standard for satellite-based land records
a modular open-source platform for building national digital identity systems
questions.e: MOSIP stands for Modular Open-Source Identity Platform. It helps countries build their own foundational ID systems without getting locked in to one vendor or to Indian systems, which is how digital sovereignty for adopters is meant to be protected. It is not a payments gateway, a land-records standard or a treaty. It illustrates India's export of the Aadhaar idea through open tools.

questions.q:
NHAI's first public Infrastructure Investment Trust was listed on the BSE in 2026. Consider the following statements about InvITs:
1. They are regulated by the Reserve Bank of India.
2. Their units cannot be listed on stock exchanges.
3. Income from assets must be retained by the trust and cannot be distributed to unit-holders.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: None is correct. InvITs are regulated by SEBI under the 2014 Regulations. Their units list on exchanges, as NHAI's did, allowing investors to take direct exposure to infrastructure. Income from tolls, rents, interest and dividends is distributed to unit-holders, which is the core attraction of the vehicle. For government agencies, they serve as an asset-monetisation route, recycling money from completed roads into new projects.

questions.q:
Under the Natural Gas (Supply Regulation) Order, 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Allocation follows a four-tier priority framework.
2. Allocation relies on consumers' average gas use over the past six months.
3. Supply to non-priority users such as power plants and petrochemical units may be curtailed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. The order rations scarce gas during the Hormuz disruption, using past use as a baseline. Gas diverted to priority sectors is sold at a newly fixed pooled price, spreading costs across users. It was issued under the Essential Commodities Act, separate from the LPG order. A High-level Committee reviews supply to other non-domestic sectors such as hospitality.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Platform : Purpose
1. MCA21 : Registry and filings of companies and LLPs
2. Udyam : MSME registration on self-declaration
3. Business Reforms Action Plan : Comparing State regulatory requirements
4. SPICe+ : Filing of monthly GST returns
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pair 4 is wrong: SPICe+ is an integrated web form for starting a business, combining incorporation, DIN, PAN, TAN and EPFO and ESIC registration. GST returns go through the GST Network. Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are right. BRAP, running since 2015, pushes States to reduce compliance burdens and now has a district version. These platforms are the core of India's digital approach to ease of doing business.

questions.q:
With reference to Digital Public Infrastructure, consider the following statements:
1. Digital Public Goods are modular building blocks that help operationalise DPI but are not DPI themselves.
2. Bhashini, an AI-led language translation platform, is cited as a Digital Public Good.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. Digital Public Goods include open-source software, open standards, open data, open AI systems and open content that respect privacy and best practice. DPI refers to the running, secure and interoperable systems that deliver services. The distinction is commonly blurred in news reports. India made this agenda central during its G20 Presidency in 2023 and now shares it with partner countries.

questions.q:
Match List-I (Platform) with List-II (Function):
List-I
A. National Single Window System
B. PARIVESH 3.0
C. e-Gram SWARAJ
D. TReDS
List-II
1. Discounting of MSME receivables through multiple financiers
2. Environmental clearances and post-approval compliance
3. Guiding investors to identify and apply for approvals
4. Gram Panchayat profiles, planning and accounting
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The National Single Window System covers Central departments and States for investor approvals. PARIVESH is the environment-related hub. e-Gram SWARAJ gives a unified view of panchayat finances, assets and planning. TReDS addresses delayed MSME payments, since invoices owed by corporates, departments and PSUs are financed through competing financiers. Separating these look-alike portals by the user they serve helps avoid confusion.

questions.q:
The theme 'Forests and Economies' drew attention to bamboo as 'green gold'. Consider the following statements:
1. The Indian Forest Act was amended in 2017 so that bamboo grown outside forest areas is not treated as a tree for felling and transit rules.
2. The Forest Rights Act, 2006 treats bamboo as minor forest produce.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. The 2017 amendment freed bamboo grown on non-forest land from felling and transit permits, which supports farmers and industry. The 2006 Act counts bamboo, tendu leaves, honey and similar items as minor forest produce, over which forest-dwellers have rights. These legal changes support the notes' argument for value chains, agroforestry and a bioeconomy based on community ownership.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 64-66; Indian Forest Amendment and FRA definition are static

questions.q:
With reference to cooperatives and the Constitution, consider the following statements:
1. The right to form cooperative societies is in Article 19(1)(c).
2. Promotion of cooperatives is a Directive Principle under Article 43B.
3. Part IXB deals with cooperative societies.
4. These provisions were added by the 97th Amendment Act, 2011.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All four are correct. The 97th Amendment gave cooperatives constitutional status through a fundamental right, a Directive Principle and a separate Part covering Articles 243ZH to 243ZT. Together they deal with incorporation, regulation and winding up. The structure aims at autonomous and democratically controlled societies, though its federal reach was later questioned because cooperatives within one State are a State subject.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Organisation : Type of cooperative
1. Kendriya Bhandar : Producers' cooperative
2. Gujarat Cooperative Milk Marketing Federation : Marketing cooperative
3. Pani-panchayats : Farming cooperative
4. APPCO : Producers' cooperative
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pair 1 is wrong: Kendriya Bhandar is a consumers' cooperative that provides goods at fair prices by bypassing middlemen. Pairs 2, 3 and 4 are right. AMUL's federation sells collectively for dairy producers; pani-panchayats and lift-irrigation societies give small farmers scale; and APPCO supplies raw materials and equipment to small producers. The functional grouping matters more than the organisation's name.

questions.q: The proposed India Semiconductor Research Centre has been compared with an institution in Taiwan that links public research with industry. That institution is the
questions.e: The Industrial Technology Research Institute is the model suggested. It is a public research body known for spinning out technology and firms. TSMC is a commercial chip foundry, itself a later outcome of this ecosystem. Academia Sinica is a general academic institution, and Hsinchu is an industrial park administration. The suggestion responds to India's need to move from assembly to core R&D and startups.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 29-30; distractors are static

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
UDAN initiative : Focus
1. Lifeline UDAN : Seaplane routes through water aerodromes
2. Krishi UDAN : Air transport of perishable farm produce
3. International UDAN : Linking State capitals and Tier-2 cities with foreign destinations
4. UDAN 5.5 : Bids covering more than 50 water bodies
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pair 1 is wrong: Lifeline UDAN carried COVID-era medical cargo to remote and island areas, while seaplanes belong to UDAN 5.5, which invited bids for more than 50 water bodies. Pairs 2, 3 and 4 are right. These sub-schemes show the regional connectivity idea being extended to agriculture, health logistics, tourism and international links within the Ministry of Civil Aviation's central sector framework.

questions.q:
Regarding the PM GatiShakti National Master Plan, consider the following statements:
1. It was launched in October 2021.
2. The Network Planning Group evaluates infrastructure projects under it.
3. It covers only Central ministries and leaves out States and Union Territories.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: all States and Union Territories are included, along with 57 Central ministries, on a shared platform of more than 1,700 data layers. Many States have also notified logistics policies, and a district module is being rolled out through Aspirational Districts. The aim is to plan multimodal connectivity together, avoiding the old pattern of departments working in isolated silos.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Programme : Associated body
1. GOBARdhan : Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen)
2. National Bio Energy Programme : Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
3. PM Ujjwala Yojana : Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 3 are right. Pair 2 is wrong: the National Bio Energy Programme is under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, with Waste to Energy and Biogas components. GOBARdhan, launched in 2018, turns organic waste into energy and manure under the sanitation mission. Cooking-fuel programmes are spread across ministries, which is why questions about who runs what often catch candidates.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 38; Shankar IAS pp. 25-27

questions.q:
Statement-I: The RBI Governor can decide a Monetary Policy Committee decision when its votes are evenly split.
Statement-II: The Committee has six members, so an equal division of votes is possible.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct and linked. With six members, a three-three split can arise, so the RBI Act gives the Governor a second or casting vote to break the tie. This also tilts ultimate control to the central bank's side, since three of the six members come from the RBI. External members bring expertise in economics, banking, finance or monetary policy.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 34; casting vote is static

questions.q: In the new GDP series, the Supply and Use Tables framework has been aligned with the national accounts mainly in order to
o: convert Indian GDP into purchasing power parity terms for global comparison
measure household consumption inequality across States
replace the Index of Industrial Production as the measure of factory output
reduce the gap between production-side and expenditure-side estimates of GDP
questions.e: Supply and Use Tables show how products are supplied, from output and imports, and how they are used, in consumption, investment and exports. Reconciling the two sides narrows the discrepancy between production and expenditure estimates. They do not replace the Index of Industrial Production, convert data to purchasing power parity, or measure inequality. Other changes in the series include GST, e-Vahan and PFMS data sources.

questions.q:
With reference to the national accounts series with base year 2022-23, consider the following statements:
1. The share of the non-financial private corporate sector in GDP rose compared with the old series.
2. Current-price GDP turned out smaller than the 2011-12 based estimates.
3. The share of manufacturing rose although its absolute size fell.
4. The IMF had earlier given India a 'C' grade for the quality of its national accounts.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is wrong: the corporate share fell, from 35.4 to 33.9 per cent of GDP in 2022-23, which partly answers criticism that the old series overstated this sector. Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. A smaller current-price GDP is unusual, since better data normally add activity, so it may correct earlier overestimation. A rising share with a falling level is possible because total GDP shrank more.

questions.q:
With reference to the gas-based economy, consider the following statements:
1. Government has set a target of 15 per cent for natural gas in the energy mix by 2030.
2. City Gas Distribution networks are authorised by the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. The share stood at only 6.2 per cent in 2025, so the target is ambitious, which is why the 2026 Distribution Order promises time-bound clearances and one harmonised framework for piped gas. The Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board awards geographical areas to city gas entities. Gas emits less than petrol, yet it remains a fossil fuel made mainly of methane.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 37; PNGRB role is static

questions.q: OpenADR, a standard discussed in the context of electrifying kitchens, is best described as a
o: safety code for cylinders used in LPG distribution
blockchain ledger recording rooftop solar sale between neighbours
star-rating label for the energy efficiency of induction hobs
two-way communication standard that lets appliances respond automatically to grid signals
questions.e: OpenADR, or Open Automated Demand Response, allows devices such as cooktops and EV chargers to shift load in response to signals. It grew out of California's 2002 energy crisis. Star labels are issued by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency, while blockchain trading is the separate peer-to-peer model, as in Lucknow. A pilot by Tata Power Delhi reported meaningful peak reductions among commercial and industrial users.

questions.q:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
1. Establishment of NABARD
2. Maclagan Committee proposal for three-tier cooperative banking
3. Establishment of the Union Ministry of Cooperation
4. Setting up of the National Cooperative Development Corporation
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The Maclagan Committee came in 1914, the National Cooperative Development Corporation in 1963, NABARD in 1982, and the Ministry of Cooperation in 2021. The order shows the movement from colonial credit design, to planned development support, to rural refinance, and finally a dedicated ministry. The vision of Sahkar se Samriddhi and the 2025 National Cooperation Policy build on this history.

questions.q:
Statement-I: In its 2021 ruling on the 97th Amendment, the Supreme Court held that Part IXB applies only to multi-State cooperative societies.
Statement-II: Cooperatives confined to one State fall in the State List, and the Amendment had not been ratified by half of the State Legislatures.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct and linked. In Union of India v. Rajendra N. Shah, the Court found that Part IXB significantly affected an exclusive State subject, Entry 32 of List II, so ratification under Article 368(2) was needed. Multi-State societies under Entry 44 of List I fall within Union competence, so the Part survives for them. This explains the Union-State uncertainty that the notes mention.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 23-25; Rajendra Shah (2021) is static

questions.q:
With reference to the Bureau of Indian Standards, consider the following statements:
1. Its genesis lies in the Indian Standards Institution of 1947.
2. It runs hallmarking for purity of gold and silver jewellery.
3. A large majority of Indian Standards are harmonised with ISO and IEC standards.
4. It functions under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 4 is wrong: BIS comes under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, a commonly missed detail. Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct, with about 94 per cent of standards harmonised. The 1986 Act created the Bureau and the 2016 Act widened it to mandatory certification and hallmarking. Harmonisation with international norms helps Indian products in foreign markets and reduces technical barriers to trade.

questions.q:
With reference to peer-to-peer power trading in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Lucknow blockchain pilot ran under a regulatory sandbox of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission.
2. The Centre's facility announced in February 2026 was placed under the BharatNet programme.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are wrong. The Lucknow pilot, led by the India Smart Grid Forum and Australia's Powerledger, ran under a sandbox of the State regulator, UPERC, which reflects the State's role in distribution. The February 2026 facility for Delhi and western Uttar Pradesh sits under the India Energy Stack. BharatNet is a rural broadband network and has no role here. Uttar Pradesh then directed utilities to provide for such trading.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 25-27; BharatNet's role is static

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Year : Use of the Essential Commodities Act
1. May 2022 : Stock limits on wheat
2. August 2022 : States told to watch tur dal stocks
3. September 2023 : Wheat stock limits with portal reporting
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pair 1 is wrong: May 2022 saw a cap of 10 million tonnes on sugar exports; wheat stock limits came only in September 2023, with portal reporting, as pair 3 says. Pair 2 is right: States were told to watch tur dal stocks after slow kharif sowing. Wheat limits were tightened in December 2023 and revised in August 2025. The March 2026 LPG and gas orders extend this old statute's crisis role to energy.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Static check-posts at State borders could be removed after GST.
Statement-II: The E-Way Bill is a single electronic document that replaced State-level permits for moving goods.
Statement-III: GST subsumed entry taxes that had been collected at such borders.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct and both explain Statement-I
Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct but only one of them explains Statement-I
Only one of Statement-II and Statement-III is correct and it explains Statement-I
Neither Statement-II nor Statement-III is correct
questions.e: Both explanations are correct and relevant. Check-posts existed mainly to collect entry-related taxes and verify documents. GST removed most such taxes, and the E-Way Bill replaced paper permits with an electronic record that can be checked on the road. Together they removed the reason for stopping trucks at borders. This reduces transit time and logistics costs, and shows how tax reform and digital systems reinforce one another.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 17-20; subsuming of entry taxes is static

questions.q:
Regarding the relaxed FDI rules for countries sharing a land border with India, consider the following statements:
1. Proposals in select sectors such as capital goods and electronics are to be cleared within 60 days.
2. In those fast-tracked proposals, majority ownership and control must stay with resident Indian citizens or Indian-owned entities.
3. Press Note 3 of 2020 had placed all such investment on the automatic route.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: speed comes with a safeguard on control, balancing capital needs and national security. Statement 3 reverses history: Press Note 3 required the Government route for all investment from land-border countries, largely with China in mind. The relaxation allows faster joint ventures and technology access for electronics and solar supply chains while retaining domestic control over companies.

questions.q:
A Parliamentary panel commented on aviation in 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. The Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024 replaced the Aircraft Act, 1934.
2. A statutory Passenger Rights Charter is already in force under the 2024 law, according to the panel.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct as a matter of settled law. Statement 2 is wrong: the panel noted that there is no statutory framework for passenger rights despite over 350 million passengers a year, and it recommended such a charter under the new Act. It also called for an independent safety committee and time-bound DGCA recruitment, as nearly half of the regulator's sanctioned posts were vacant.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 30-32; Aircraft Act replacement is static

questions.q:
With reference to Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), consider the following statements:
1. They form the base tier of the short-term cooperative credit structure.
2. They are barred from activities other than lending, to protect their credit function.
3. Each is directly licensed as a bank by the RBI.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct: PACS lend at village level as the base of the short-term cooperative credit structure. Statement 2 is wrong: many now run petrol and diesel outlets, PM Jan Aushadhi Kendras and fertiliser services, and over 30,000 work as Common Service Centres. Statement 3 is wrong: they are societies registered under State laws and are not licensed as banks, unlike State and district cooperative banks. Computerisation of about 63,000 PACS aims to strengthen them further.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 23-25; three-tier position and licensing are static

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's gas economy:
1. India produces most of the LPG it needs at home.
2. India's underground gas storage is on the same scale as Europe's.
3. India imports its entire natural gas requirement as LNG.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: None holds. India imports about 60 per cent of its LPG. It has limited LNG storage, unlike Europe's underground storage, so gas is used soon after regasification. About half of its gas demand is met domestically, with Qatar supplying nearly half of the imported LNG. These facts explain why the crisis quickly reached kitchens and factories, though some users could switch to naphtha or furnace oil.

questions.q:
Regarding the implementation of the BHAVYA scheme, consider the following statements:
1. The National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation is the implementing agency.
2. The developer SPV is formed between the National Industrial Corridor Development and Implementation Trust and the State nodal agency.
3. Parks with private developers get a higher ceiling of support per acre than other eligible projects.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: private-developer parks get up to Rs 50 lakh per acre or 50 per cent of infrastructure cost, whichever is lower, which is less than the Rs 1 crore ceiling for other eligible projects. The SPV owns the assets and handles planning, construction and maintenance. A State or Central PSU acts as sponsor, and the design links with PM GatiShakti.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Refinery products carry the largest weight within the Index of Core Industries.
2. The Index of Industrial Production is compiled and released by the Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: refinery products outweigh the other seven core industries. Statement 2 confuses two indices: the Office of the Economic Adviser in DPIIT releases the core index, while the Index of Industrial Production comes from the National Statistics Office under MoSPI. The eight core industries together make up about 40 per cent of the industrial production index, so core output is a useful lead indicator.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 34; IIP publisher is static

questions.q:
Statement-I: Formalisation recorded in the accounts may overstate welfare gains if small firms simply close.
Statement-II: India's national accounts tend to rely on organised-sector filings that are easier to measure, and informal activity is harder to capture.
Statement-III: Current-price GDP in the new series came out larger than earlier estimates.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct and both explain Statement-I
Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct but only one of them explains Statement-I
Only one of Statement-II and Statement-III is correct and it explains Statement-I
Neither Statement-II nor Statement-III is correct
questions.e: Statement-III is wrong because the new series was about 3 to 4 per cent smaller. Statement-II is correct and explains the first: when output moves from a small shop to a large firm, accounts built on visible filings record gain, while the loss of the kirana shop goes unseen. Critics say this makes the issue democratic as well as technical. Better informal-sector surveys are the suggested remedy.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Term : Meaning
1. Prosumer : A household that both produces and consumes power
2. Virtual power plant : Distributed loads and generation run as one unit
3. Peer-to-peer trading : Households selling electricity to one another
4. Time-of-use tariff : A single flat price across all hours
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pair 4 is wrong: time-of-use tariffs vary by hour, raising peak prices to encourage shifting. Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are right. A household with rooftop solar and a battery can store daytime surplus for evening cooking. Aggregating many such units can provide grid services, and trading at feeder level, as in the Lucknow pilot, can turn a neighbourhood into a micro virtual power plant.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT among the four schemes described under the India Semiconductor Mission?
questions.e: The four schemes listed are Semiconductor Fabs, Display Fabs, Compound Semiconductors with ATMP and OSAT, and the Design Linked Incentive. Critical mineral recycling belongs to a separate policy track under the Mines Ministry. The structure shows the ambition to cover the chain from design to manufacturing to packaging. ISM 2.0 was announced in the Union Budget 2026-27, with the talent pipeline supported by Chips to Start-up.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Guarantee arrangement : Feature
1. CGSMFI-2.0 : Guarantees to lenders that fund MFIs for on-lending to small borrowers
2. Mutual Credit Guarantee Scheme : A Centrally Sponsored Scheme implemented through State governments
3. National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company : Wholly owned by the Reserve Bank of India
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Only pair 1 is right: in CGSMFI-2.0 the cover goes to Member Lending Institutions that fund MFIs, not directly to end borrowers. Pair 2 is wrong: the Mutual Credit Guarantee Scheme is a Central Sector Scheme giving a 60 per cent guarantee on MSME loans for machinery and equipment. Pair 3 is wrong: the trustee company that manages both schemes is wholly owned by the Department of Financial Services in the Finance Ministry, not by the RBI.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The MEIS was replaced by a scheme remitting embedded taxes and duties on exports.
Statement-II: The WTO had held MEIS to be inconsistent with international trade rules.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct and linked. MEIS gave rewards tied to exports, which amounted to a prohibited export subsidy under WTO rules. RoDTEP was designed to be compatible because it merely refunds embedded central, state and local levies not refunded under any other mechanism. The principle is that taxes should not be exported, while a subsidy for exporting is not allowed.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Term : Description
1. LPG : Mainly propane and butane
2. LNG : Mainly methane cooled to about minus 160 degrees Celsius
3. Regasification : Step that turns LNG back into gas at terminals
4. JKM : European benchmark for crude oil
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pair 4 is wrong: JKM, the Japan-Korea Marker, is the Asian spot benchmark for LNG. Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are right. LPG comes from natural gas streams and crude refining, while LNG is shipped in carriers to cryogenic tanks, regasified and sent through pipelines. The press often merges the two fuels, but their sources, uses and risks are different.

questions.q:
Critics of India's statistics system have cited some episodes. Consider the following statements:
1. The Consumption Survey of 2017-18 was not released after reportedly showing a fall in household spending.
2. Delay in the Census has not affected policy, as all allocations already use fresh population data.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: policy still relies on 2011 population data, which is the criticism. The 2019 labour force controversy, with resignations from the National Statistical Commission, is another cited episode. Critics argue that statistics are public infrastructure and that the accounts tilt towards measurable formal firms, missing informal distress after demonetisation, GST and COVID-19.

questions.q:
Regarding the second edition of the Fiscal Health Index, consider the following statements:
1. Unlike the first edition, it also covers North-Eastern and Himalayan States.
2. North-Eastern and Himalayan States are ranked along with major States in one common list.
3. It relies on data from the Comptroller and Auditor General.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: the first edition covered only 18 major States, while this one adds 10, using CAG data for 2023-24. Statement 2 is wrong: those States are ranked separately in three groups, with refined sub-indicators to reflect difficult terrain, limited own revenue and dependence on Union transfers. The ranking is meant to encourage competitive federalism, since States hold about one-third of general government debt.

questions.q:
Regarding India's strategic petroleum reserves, consider the following statements:
1. They are held in underground rock caverns, usually near the coast.
2. They are managed by the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation as part of its commercial stocks.
3. Their capacity alone already satisfies the IEA's 90-day benchmark.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct: crude is held in underground rock caverns, usually near the coast. Statement 2 is wrong: a special purpose vehicle, Indian Strategic Petroleum Reserves Ltd, set up in 2004 under the Petroleum Ministry, manages them, and they are additional to oil companies' commercial stocks. Statement 3 is wrong: the 5.33 MMT capacity covers only about 9.5 days of crude, far below the IEA's 90-day benchmark, and there is no clear release policy.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Mass adoption of induction cooking may steepen India's evening electricity peak.
Statement-II: Demand already peaks around 9 to 11 p.m., a period overlapping with household dinner cooking.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct and linked. Cooking loads would add to an evening peak, forcing distribution companies to buy expensive spot power, run gas plants, use storage or shed load. So the policy question is how to electrify and not merely whether to. Automated demand response, time-of-use tariffs and rooftop solar with batteries are suggested as ways of flattening this peak.

questions.q:
With reference to the UDAN scheme, consider the following statements:
1. It flows from the National Civil Aviation Policy, 2016.
2. The Airports Authority of India is its implementing agency.
3. Landing and parking charges are waived at selected airports.
4. Participating States cut VAT on aviation turbine fuel to one per cent or less.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All four are correct. The scheme works through Viability Gap Funding, airfare caps and a shared effort among the Centre, States and airport operators. State tax cuts and fee waivers lower airline costs so that thin routes can work. The Parliamentary panel's concern is sustainability: many awarded routes were discontinued, and there is no structured exit strategy after support ends.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Cooperative entity : Regulatory position
1. Urban cooperative bank : Banking regulation by the RBI
2. Multi-State cooperative society : Oversight by the Central Registrar
3. Single-State cooperative society : Oversight by the State Registrar
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: All three are right. Cooperative banks come under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 for banking functions, with NABARD supervising rural ones. Multi-State societies are governed by the 2002 Act and the Central Registrar, and single-State societies by State Acts. Dual control of urban cooperative banks by a Registrar and the RBI remains a cited weakness, along with high NPAs and political interference in elections.

questions.q:
Under the statutory flexible inflation targeting framework, consider the following statements:
1. The RBI Governor is the ex-officio chairperson of the Monetary Policy Committee.
2. Failure means inflation outside the band for two consecutive quarters.
3. Three external members are appointed by the Central Government.
4. One RBI officer on the Committee is nominated by the RBI's Central Board.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 2 is wrong: failure means three consecutive quarters outside the band. Statements 1, 3 and 4 give the six-member structure, with the Deputy Governor in charge of monetary policy as the remaining member. The framework came from the Urjit Patel Committee and was given legal force by amending the RBI Act in 2016. The Committee fixes the policy rate needed to meet the target.

questions.q: Viability Gap Funding in infrastructure schemes such as UDAN is best described as
o: a tax on profitable routes that is credited to a separate national fund
an equity stake taken by the Union Government in private operators
a concessional loan from the RBI that is repayable when a project breaks even
a grant that bridges the gap between a project's expected revenue and what makes it commercially workable
questions.e: Viability Gap Funding is non-repayable public support where social or strategic value exceeds what users can pay. In UDAN it goes to airlines on awarded routes so that capped fares remain possible. It is neither a loan nor an equity stake, though a route levy has supported such funding in the past. Without a plan for when support ends, routes may close, which is the panel's concern.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 30-32; VGF definition is static

questions.q:
With reference to NBFC-MFIs, consider the following statements:
1. They are permitted to accept public deposits.
2. At least 75 per cent of their total assets must be microfinance loans.
3. Microfinance loans are collateral-free loans to households with annual income up to Rs 3 lakh.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is wrong: an NBFC-MFI is a non-deposit-taking company, so it relies on borrowings from banks and others. This is why a guarantee to lenders matters. Statements 2 and 3 are correct and define the category. Microfinance supports inclusion without mandatory collateral, and women make up nearly all borrowers according to the Economic Survey 2025-26. The income limit decides what counts as a qualifying loan.

questions.q:
The Union Budget 2026-27 announced a Coconut Promotion Scheme. Consider the following statements:
1. The crop grows mainly within 23 degrees north and south of the Equator.
2. It grows from sea level up to about 600 metres.
3. Annual rainfall of about 1,000 to 2,500 mm suits it.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct, describing a tropical, humid crop suited to well-drained sandy loam, laterite and coastal alluvium. Temperatures of 20 to 32 degrees Celsius suit it too. India produces nearly 30 per cent of world output, led by Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka. The scheme aims to rejuvenate old and unproductive gardens, and to expand cultivation along the coasts.
